utterances.text: Well, it was like this: I completed my work on the 18th of December and continued working in the project bureau. On the 6th of January, the report was completed, the text of it, the textual part at the beginning. And all the maps with the various designations of category for the damages and the location of the damages came at the end, so probably sometime between the 18th of December and the 6th of January, that's when I took a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember having looked through all the minutes, all the notes you took once they had been typed out?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have had to have done that. I must have done that because I signed it ultimately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when they gave it back to you, you took the minutes or the notes and signed it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I gave -- I signed it when I gave a statement to the investigators, which was in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you sign the report when, as you say, you read through the report to verify it when your name is at the bottom of every report, of each of these minutes or notes?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. That's not what we did. We didn't do it like that at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal, and attached to that statement was this material that I worked on in 1991. So as all this went together, I verified it, authorised it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you do that in 1991?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that's not what we did. What you would have to do was to call all these individuals. Some of them weren't employees of the institute, and you would have to call them and sign them, and it was assumed that the teams working on the assignment were doing their work conscientiously and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anything to debate there. I assume they read through what had been typed out.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anything to debate there either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why didn't they sign their part, their portion of the report?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why we didn't sign in 1991? Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we just didn't sign it. That wasn't customary. I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some -- anyone sign, anybody?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you signed this in the year 2000; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you sign then?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the forms attached here? I think the forms that are attached here are the signed ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it comprised work on 50 structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you sign then in 2000 and not in 1991?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that's what I was asked to do. If it is attached to my statement, then I sign it because that was what I was required to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after a period of nine years, after nine years had gone by, could you remember all of the damages in the insulae number nine, ten, eleven, twelve?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write my report nine years later, I wrote my report immediately after the damage was incurred, but I signed to say that they were mine. Nine years later I can't remember all the damages, especially after ten major projects that have been ongoing to reconstruct buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how do you know nine years later that what has been typed out and what the reports contain are the authentic facts that you set out in your report?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they are the same reports. In the text itself, I can recognise my own method of writing and compiling a report, and I know that what I said there was what happened, was what I actually did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you looked at it in the year 2000, you recognised that that was what you had done in 1991. And I assume that you remember what the contents of the report were.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I read it. Not in great detail, but I read it and I established that that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that in 2000? For example, if I ask you today what exactly were the damages on various buildings, can you remember all of it without looking at the documents?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember some things, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Give me any example except for the Franciscan Monastery. Do you remember any other damage on any other building that you wrote about here?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well. For example, the Church of the Holy Saviour, right by the Franciscan Monastery. This is a Renaissance church, one of the most valuable monuments in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me what the damage is.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is indirect, the damage is indirect, but this is a building on which this damage is terrible. It can basically not be redressed. It's on the surface of the wall, then also on the ornaments around the entrance door and then also on the plasters, and some of them were even dislocated. The building was not hit directly, but the facade and the external wall was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the category?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The category of damage could be third category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now like to look a page?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all in the B/C/S version, the last three figures are 150, and then page 151.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at page 150 first. Does number 11 indicate the church that you just talked about?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please look at page 151.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said to us that you established that the roof was damaged there. Is that what you said a few minutes ago in respect of the Church of Our Saviour?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was minor damage that was caused by the hit of a rather powerful projectile that hit a building. It's number 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my question. Did you say that you established that the roof of the Church of Our Saviour was damaged? Is that what you said two minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes or no. Did you say it or did you not say it?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any damage on the roof that is indicated here?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not indicated here. I probably considered this to be a lesser damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you mention that today, 14 years later, and not in your report, the one that you made ten days after it?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably considered it to be a lesser damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I would ask my learned friend when he's putting the questions to the witness and asserting that points were not made X number of years ago, to be accurate in the way the question is phrased. I would like to refer, perhaps for Your Honours' convenience, to the English translation of this particular subsite, which can be found at L0060310.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I was talking about two drawings. I haven't come to that page yet, my learned friend. I will get to that page too, but I haven't got to that page yet. And in the English translations there are no sketches, only in the B/C/S version. I'm still talking about sketches only, and I will get to the page you've referred to just now. Then I'm going to indicate both the B/C/S and the English versions of that particular page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: My only point being, Your Honours, that X number of years ago, when this report was prepared back in 1991, there was mention of damage to the rooftops. It's not correct to put it to the witness that she did not talk about damage to the roof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kaufman. The point, Mr. Petrovic, appears to be that the detailed report prepared by the witness does mention such damage. What you are identifying is a summarising sketch that was put at the beginning of the report, no doubt by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's precisely what I wished to show. I wished to indicate the difference between what the sketch, the map shows, and what the distinguished witness said. That was the aim of what I was trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Can I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Peko, were you wanting to say something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would just like to point out that a few minutes ago I said that I think that it was the third category of damage. That means either one or the other. That is to say either the facade, the front wall, or the roof. I estimated that the facade, the front wall, sustained major damage and the roof sustained minor damage. And now what I wrote --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, the map on 151 is not accurate. Does it reflect what you said?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 152, it does reflect that where category 3 damage is concerned, that is to say either/or; either the wall or the roof. I may have mentioned the roof, but obviously I considered the damage sustained by the front wall to be major damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the damage that you're referring to, is that an indirect hit?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the wall?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, please look at 151 and tell me where is an indirect hit shown here.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the dotted line. And this dotted line is there, right by the front wall on the south and partly the eastern wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not on the building itself?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no other way of depicting it. That is how we did it, with the dotted line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Thank you. Tell me, when did you -- when did you establish how a particular building was damaged? You don't have to look at these papers any more now. I'm giving you a general question. When did you establish when the building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When touring it, when coming to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, at any point in time did you have any knowledge about the previous status of the building that you were reviewing?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What previous status do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to explain. Did you know in what condition the building was before you went out there? For example, let's put it this way: Before October 1991, did you know in what condition these buildings were or a particular building was?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this church, for instance, the Church of Our Saviour, that's a church that we pass by practically every day so we are constantly aware of it. So the damage sustained by stone on our monuments is obvious because new damage can easily be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Domino 6 in insula 12. Do you know in what condition it was before you actually investigated?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six? I'd have to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm asking you whether you knew when you entered that building in what condition it had been before 1991. Did you know?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot identify the building exactly. Do you really think that I go into all of those 50 buildings, 50 houses every day? You see, damage is quite obvious. I told you at the very outset that what is important for me is to distinguish between a direct hit and an indirect hit. A cultural monument is important for me as such. I don't know how to put this. And at the moment when I arrive there, I see there is damage and I can distinguish between old damage and new damage, recent damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you distinguish between an old and a new crack in the wall?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that can be seen. Very often these cracks in our walls are covered with paint, and when due to vibrations and due to hits there are further cracks, they appear in the same place. Cracks are activated. That is the word we use. And that is where the plaster falls off, the mortar falls off if cracks are reactivated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know when there were cracks for years, for a long time, and then it becomes bigger? Why did this not happen in September 1991? How come you know it wasn't in September?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in September there wasn't any new hit. Why would that happen?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that all buildings were in perfect condition until October 1991?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not mean that they were in perfect condition, but I can recognise a crack being activated, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that between the earthquake of 1979 and 1991 a crack could not have happened?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, hardly, because if that were the case, then all buildings would have fallen apart. If they were cracks coming up all the time, then they'd fall apart. So it's vibrations, detonations, that kind of thing causes cracks. Of any origin, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was it that you knew in terms of damage sustained by various buildings apart from the Church of Our Saviour and the Franciscan Monastery? What did you know about all the other buildings and the condition they were in before October 1991?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The condition they were in? Well, that they were in proper physical condition, that they were usable, that they were being used, and that the people living and working there were taking care of them, as is customary in our part of the world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can it be assumed that, when you did not enter 95 per cent of these buildings, because these are residential buildings or business premises, how can you claim that they were being maintained properly when you were never entered them?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those that are in poor condition become part of a reconstruction programme or renewal programme. After the earthquake, buildings were restored and renewed according to a certain programme. The Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments could have data about this. And also we have a reconstruction institute in Dubrovnik too that was established precisely after the earthquake of 1979. It was engaged in systematic reconstruction of buildings in town as an investor. As I said, from 1988, I was employed in the bureau called Arhitekt. I worked on four buildings, on four buildings that were damaged during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my questions. That's what I'm asking you about. So there is information, there is data about this at the institute, and so on and so forth. So when you are at a building, you do not really know anything about it, because all this information is registered somewhere at the institute. But what do you know about it? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I'm some kind of an expert. I can absolutely distinguish between old damage and recent damage. I cannot say our buildings are in ideal condition, but I can distinguish between old damage and recent damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you distinguish, for example, recent, new damage on a new building? I mean, I'm not asking you about roofs, I'm asking you about walls?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Front walls you mean, facades?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, inside, within a building, a particular floor.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't that frequent that there was damage there. In nine buildings, there was total damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my question. I'm not asking you about nine buildings, I'm asking you how you can distinguish between new damage and old damage sustained by the floor in a particular building. How can you tell?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the floor there was damage very seldom except in the case of these nine buildings that were totally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no constructional damage in -- except for the roof damage?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was damage on the front walls, the facades, then the roofs, so that is part of the construction, too, yes. Most of the constructional damage could be noticed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in one of the same buildings, how do you distinguish between damage sustained in October and November and December respectively?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not asked to do that. I was asked to register all the damage that was sustained on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that includes all the damage from the months of October, November, and December.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This preliminary report refers to those three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point yesterday you mentioned Davorin Rudolf.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he spoke over the radio.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what he said?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just know that his voice had an incredibly pacifying effect, and his wish was to make the inhabitants of Dubrovnik feel calmer and help them live through this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember whether he referred to an individual called Jokic, Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he referred to anyone in particular. I'm not sure. I'm not sure. I think that he addressed us in a very humane way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that he conveyed the apology that the JNA addressed to him and the citizens of Dubrovnik because of what was going on at that time in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: An apology. I don't remember. That would have been a paradox.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps that he said that this Admiral Jokic had been called back to Belgrade to see the Federal Secretary for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you if I told you that Mr. Rudolf himself says that that is what he spoke about?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I listened to Mr. Rudolf with great delight, because he calmed us down in a way, but do I not remember all of this, but after all, it is for him to speak about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although I know that this is a traumatic and hard experience for you, I will have to ask you something about the building that you were in. Please don't hold it against me. This is simply in line with the role I have before this Court. Tell me, when was the building that you were staying at hit?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 11.00 and 12.00 on the 6th of December. I don't know when exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how it was hit?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what my husband said, it was a guided rocket. I know the exact point of impact, and I know that I saw white traces. I know that early the following morning I went to collect stone that had fallen off that building. This was important for me because the city cleaning services were already cleaning the streets, and it was important for this particular building, and that's when I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the damage involved?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile hit the corner of the building or, rather, the eastern wall, right below the stone drainpipe. The surface of the wall was destroyed. Perhaps one square metre was destroyed, and about one metre of the stone drainpipe along with the adjoining ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the total surface area, would you say, of the damage?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to the facade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the damage you saw to the building you lived in.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the facade, the surface area might have been between one and two metres. It's at the corner of the building. But what was damaged most was the roof, because the whole structure was displaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a look at a photograph now for me, please, in the first binder before you. 01069400 is the number. The photograph is from the B/C/S bundle, it doesn't exist in the English bundle. 400 are the last three digits. 4-0-0 are the last three digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher place it on the overhead projector, please. That will help us all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Peko, would you please take a look at the photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is that your house? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the photograph back, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, after looking at the photograph, would you say that that was a two-metre wide by one metre damage? Would that be the surface area?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the eastern side and on the northern side is where the damage is. Now, on the northern facade, the pieces of stone have been dislodged. If you know -- if one knows that the stones are 25 to 30 centimetres high, each stone block, you have one, two, three, four, four blocks, then I think that my assessment is roughly correct. And there's a piece of stone missing at the level of the drainpipe. So I would say I was correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the page ending in the 399, and in English it is 0061069 is the ERN English number. Madam, would you read what your colleague wrote about the damage. Or, rather, tell me first, please, whether that is your building, the one mentioned here. Is that the house you were in, in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Block Boskoviceva 15. Yes, that's the house, that's the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at what it says in the report there for the structure, and does that correspond to what you've just told us?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Direct hit into the stone drainpipe. Direct hit in the roof drainpipe on the eastern and northern facade which caused lesser damages to the stone channel about 20 -- stone canal, about 20 centimetres, and a stone console or support."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does it say next?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the northern facade, a stone block has been blown away and ten others damaged."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, your assessments and your testimony and what it says here, can you see that there is a significant difference between your assessment and what it says there? Do you agree that there is quite a lot of difference between your description and the description made by Mr. Elakovic and Comor?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to damages to other structures, this is indeed a lesser damage, but I assume that the damage does correspond with the surface area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you concentrate on my question, please. Do you agree that there is a great difference between your description of the damages and what Comor and Elakovic ascertained?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see no great difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a difference in the dimensions, in the size of the damage? It says 20 centimetres here and you said one to two metres, I believe, which means ten times more, madam.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this to you. This is a direct description of what was damaged by the hit. The canal, or drainpipe, was considerably damaged, but I don't think there's a great difference in surface area, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell us as to the dimensions of the damage a moment ago on the building you lived in? What did you tell us five minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five minutes ago I told you the exact spot at which the impact hit. And to the best of my recollections, that is 12 or 13 years later. This is something that my colleagues saw, and this is a photograph. So it is facts from them, supplied by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was the house you were in?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say -- just a moment, please. Is it logical and natural that in the house that you were living in that you remember exactly, because you were very interested in what was going on because you and your family were housed there, wasn't it logical that this was something that stuck in your memory?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did stick in my memory, you're right. It stuck there and lodged very firmly. However, at the time I viewed it as damage to a structure, and I knew exactly what I would have to do after the war, which was to repair. So I accepted that as a fact. It never entered my head to take up a measuring stick and measure the area. And I know that much more extensive repairs would have to be done than what it says here, let alone the roof construction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you approach in the same way the structures where you had the duty and responsibility of assessing the material damage -- the damage?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That cannot be compared at all. I was an ordinary citizen, inhabitant there who, through force of circumstance, managed to survive the hit, because the building was far more sensitive in other places than that particular place where the shell hit. So I cannot at all times look at things professionally and act as a professional. Otherwise, I would have come here with a measuring stick to measure the table in front of you, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What equipment did you have when you went to investigate on site, except the form you told us about?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A pencil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't have a tape-measure? You didn't have a camera? You didn't have a notebook to record the damage? You didn't have any of that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well what architectural investigation requires. It requires a lot of time and effort, and there are certain areas where you -- which are inaccessible, where you would need scaffolding to be able to assess the damage. Of course I had a measuring -- a tape-measure. I forgot to mention that. Because I looked at the depth of the impact, the damage. But had we used a tape-measure to measure each and every piece of damage, that would have been impossible. I know -- knew that investigations would follow and that repair work would have to be done and that would come afterwards, but detailed procedure in that way, where would that have led us? We would have been spending years and years doing that. It's just not reasonable to assume that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After my question you said you had a tape-measure. To begin with you just told us you had a pencil, and that seemed to you to be illogical so you added the tape measure, is that it?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for my mistake, my omission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use your tape-measure to measure, the one you said you took with you?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always take a tape-measure with me in order to measure things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you measure?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The diameter and radius of the damage, the depth of the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what would you do on one particular structure? There were measurements to be taken everywhere, I assume.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm an architect. I can assess a dimension in space, at least roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So many damages were assessed by you visually. By looking at the structure, you would say that is one or two metres, roughly. Am I right in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Architectural measurement is a process that you're probably not acquainted with but it is a lengthy process. Architectural assessment at a ten metre height is impossible to do, and that's why we did not engage in systematic monitoring and measurement. I went to four burnt down buildings at a height of 14 metres and assessed the damage there. I can tell you which those structures were and I can tell you how long that kind of investigation lasted, but in this particular case we were not able to apply these things for our preliminary report and our preliminary assessments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to take a look at the second binder that you have before you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Petrovic, if you're moving to another, it would be convenient to have a break before we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, quite, thank you. I should have thought of that myself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Peko, before the break I asked you to take a look at a document, the second binder, to look at insula 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the page number is, in the B/C/S, 010169632, and for the English translation it is L0061497. So from that page onwards I shall be asking some questions with respect to Mrs. Peko's report in that portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Peko, insula 11 is what we're looking at, from page 632, those being the last three digits. Have you found it? Have you found the page?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, first of all you see this column headed "Type of projectile," and there is a mortar shell, 120 millimetres, three of those. How were you able to ascertain that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I assume I saw them lined up in the building, the remnants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what does a 120-millimetre shell look like?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never saw the whole of it, just the fragments that were left behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what do the fragments of a 120-millimetre shell look like?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it looks like a sort of full barrel with wing-like structures at the end. That is the fragment, that's what remains of a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the shrapnel of a 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't distinguish between a 120-millimetre shrapnel and an 82-millimetre shrapnel, but of the shrapnels that I saw, I can describe them in this way: They are pieces of steel with fragmented edges and a flat surface, on a flat surface, the torn edges, and you can see this flat plate-like surface.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you distinguish between shrapnel of 82-millimetre shells and 120-millimetre shells? And did you see the remains of the wings of a mortar shell in each of these structures?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, almost in all of them. People would save them and store them away and then show -- show them to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would you find the fragments of a mortar shell? Somebody would give them to you or what?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were sort of all lined up in part of the space, apartment, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't find any of the shrapnel fragments at the spot they fell.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. People cleared up the streets the very next day and would come across these fragments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all these shell fragments were moved from the actual spot at which they fell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how can you distinguish between the remains of an 82-mortar shell and a 120-millimetre shell when it comes to these wing-like structures? Can you describe what one looks and the other looks like and what the difference is?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is in the radius, and I was able to see when it was an 82-millimetre one and a 120-millimetre one. So that's mostly it. In the structures that I investigated. And in our three-member team or commission, when I was working with my colleagues who had undergone a certain amount of training and were better versed in these matters than I was, then they would make the assessment and record it, because I really don't understand matters of that type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all the reports that you signed, you made the assessments as to what size shell had caused the damage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my duty either to make the evaluation myself or to receive information from the owner or user of the building, or even to bring in the projectile itself. But very often they didn't let us take the projectiles away, the ones that they had managed to collect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a 60-millimetre projectile, for example? Or have you ever seen a projectile from some other artillery weapon and not from a mortar?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already told you that I could recognise these remnants from an 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre mortar. Then also I could see when it was an incendiary shell that fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I also saw the traces of guided rockets. I cannot distinguish between other things. I am not an expert, an arms expert. I actually find this repulsive. I don't really want to know anything about such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a building that was indirectly hit? What did you find there?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ascertain that there had been an indirect hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find? What kind of shell remains did you find in a building that had been indirectly hit? What would you find there?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: People mostly kept larger parts of projectiles, not smaller ones usually. Since the damage sustained by buildings was mainly external, on walls, roofs, et cetera, then this would fall into the street and it would be cleaned the very next day, these tiny little fragments. Nobody collected them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find this part with the wing-like structures by the buildings that were indirectly hit?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not find them at all by buildings that were hit. Outside, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did you then establish, in the case of a building that was indirectly hit, the type and calibre of projectile that it had been hit with?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information that we would get from people living or working in the buildings. Usually when a building was hit directly, then its next-door building would be indirectly hit, the building next door, the roof on the building next door. The people who were directly hit, whose building was directly hit, would know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would people know the type and calibre of projectile?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you. At their homes they had their -- these remains. And they know. If it hit the front wall of the neighbour's house and then if their building was affected, it was probably from that building, too, but possibly there was shrapnel flying all over the place. It's hard to tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to -- for damage to be incurred by other weapons, not only mortars?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for example, a cannon, a recoilless gun, if you know what that is.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a howitzer? Could a howitzer have caused damaged?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly. I assumed that as far as these guns and cannons are concerned, there was a larger distance involved, but I'm not familiar with these weapons, and I don't know what their shells look like. I told you at the very outset, I can distinguish between a direct hit and an indirect hit, but for me that is a weapon, a weapon that caused damage. So one shell was one too many in Dubrovnik, and a crime, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, every report of yours contains precise details concerning the type of projectile that caused the damage. I'm not asking you all of this for any other reason but because of the fact that it is included in your report. There was not a single report of yours without giving the type and calibre of projectile. That's why I'm putting these questions to you. There's no other reason.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information that I would get in different ways; by seeing what the remains were at a particular building or by getting a description from the tenants, or by having the projectile brought in as such. So it was one of these types of information. I really didn't invent any of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether these remains that were shown to you were really from that building or were they perhaps from another building?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not carried around that way that they would collect ten projectiles in one building and then that they would boast with it as if it were a trophy. I don't think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know, madam, that somebody was not carrying fragments of projectiles from one building to another and yet another one? How can you know that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that many people collected these sad trophies in the town of Dubrovnik for their own collections?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: People kept this in their buildings, especially if their building had been hit by one. How many people there were who were involved in this kind of collecting is something I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to a building that was indirectly hit. What do you find by way of traces coming from a shell so that you could ascertain that it was hit by an 82-millimetre or 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tell you that the damage has to do with a projectile, a shell that hit another place near that building. For example, if you see on the facade of the Church of Our Saviour evident signs of damage, that is to say holes in the wall, they are quite pronounced even today. And you have accurate reports in terms of the damage sustained by the main street, Placa, and you see that three or four projectiles, whatever, fell on the Onofrijeva Fountain. Then they ricocheted from there in all directions. The roofs and the window frames and the walls were hit. That can be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that you actually could not ascertain with any degree of certitude the type of projectile that had hit the buildings? You did not have any direct knowledge, you did not have the necessary knowledge to establish this anyway, and you did not have the mechanisms involved.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I could tell them apart by way of their diameter and also the fragments left of 82-millimetre and 120-millimetre shells. I could distinguish between those, no doubt. And people would show them to me. I would not find them on the spot right by the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect of a building that was hit by shrapnel, how could you establish what the calibre of the original shell was?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if in the immediate neighbourhood there was a 120-millimetre shell that fell, then I know it came from there. So if it ricocheted off that wall or this wall, then I know it came from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been from a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A bigger calibre machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what you said. I don't see how come there could be machine-guns in Dubrovnik. Maybe you were doing it from up there. Maybe there were machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could you please have this last sentence interpreted to you very precisely, because it contains an insult, an insult addressed at General Strugar, and I would like the Chamber to reprimand the witness for saying such offensive words like maybe I was up there on Mount Srdj. "[In English] You were doing it from up there." [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is offence, that's an insult, and I would kindly ask you to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I don't understand what was said in the way that you do. Firstly, I see nothing addressed to your client. Secondly, when you put to the witness, "Could it have been a machine-gun?" she reacted by saying, "Well, you might know whether there was a machine-gun or not," I think addressed to you, not your client, and saying that if you're suggesting there was a machine-gun that must be your suggestion, not hers. So I'm afraid I don't concur with your interpretation of what was said. I think you may have misunderstood what was intended.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept everything you said. All right. Let's not dwell on it any longer, although, regrettably, I think that it was otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know anything about the way in which an 82-millimetre or 120-millimetre shell is fragmentised?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is anything written on the small wing-like structures that you claim you found at various buildings?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was possible to read the calibre and the year of manufacture on some, but on others, no. I cannot say that with any certitude. I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see the wing-like structures on a rifle grenade?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about descent angles of mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your teams, was there a crime investigation technician who could ascertain this type of damage?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, on our team there were men who had undergone certain training. Also, just before work started on this report, there was a brief review of the types of projectiles that could be encountered. These fragments of projectiles were on a table. However, I got involved in this later, that is to say on the 9th of December. I saw the table, and -- but I mean I really did not have any wish to look at it any further. Now, what was it I've been trying to say? Yes. We were actually warned that if we would find fragments of projectiles that there was this so-called fuse that had not exploded and that we should be very careful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you whether you had a crime investigation technician with you.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there on your team with you a ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my team at the buildings? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any such expert on the team -- on the entire team that was working on the entirety of the preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any such name, because I know most of these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a crime investigation carried out? Did anybody collect these remains of projectiles so that they could be processed afterwards in terms of crime investigation?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at page 01069635.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English translation that is page L0061498.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These reports that are marked insula 11, report 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, all the way up to -- all the way up to page 01069648, are all of those reports yours?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time is required for examining one building, for instance?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the size of the building and the extent of damage involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, give me an approximation, please. What would be the least amount of time required, and what would be the longest amount of time required?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that exactly now. I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time is needed for carrying an on-site investigation of an apartment building in the street of Miha Pracata, for instance? That is insula 11, buildings 5 and 6. How much time is required?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, Miha Pracata Street, yes, there it is. Number 1, and that is page 635, residential building, if I was there at 10.00, and then I was at the neighbouring building at 11.30, well -- 11.15. Fifteen minutes, up to one hour. I don't know how much. I'm just saying all this off-the-cuff. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me how you managed within four hours on the 15th of December to examine 11 buildings. Between 10.00 a.m. and 2.00 p.m., you examined 14 buildings. How did you manage to do that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are probably smaller buildings with less damage involved. This is a part of town that was affected in a minor way, but I don't see where this is leading to, but okay, never mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you really have enough time within four hours to actually examine buildings, 11 buildings?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eleven?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 11/2, 11/3, 11-4, 11-5, 11-6, 11-7, 11-8, 11-9, 11-12, 11-13. You managed to do all of that within four hours' time. How come?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree it was quick but did you do it properly? Did you do it accurately?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand behind this. I stand by it and I think it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these four hours, did you establish that there were 11 direct hits by 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eleven?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, 11. Believe me, I added them all up, and you can do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the place the damage took place, the size of the building, the number of damages, lots of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it true that you, in the space of four hours, were able to establish 11 mortar hits with a 120-millimetre shell? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly established the number of hits. Now, whether that took place within the space of four hours, I don't know. Perhaps I didn't record the time precisely. It's not the hour of impact, it's not anything like that. Perhaps I wasn't precise enough in determining the overall time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you were imprecise in the counting of the hits.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that to be the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a single spot where the -- and I'm talking about insula 11, the spot -- did you see the spot where the projectile actually hit the soil, the ground, or the structure?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are indirect hits and direct hits, so quite obviously I did see the direct hits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the space of those four hours, did you manage to establish and take a look at, in addition to the 11 hits, the five indirect hits as well with the 120-millimetre mortar shell? All in the space of four hours did you manage to do that too?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could, I was able to. Let me give you an example. Within the space of one minute, I was able to ascertain the damage on the cloister of the Franciscan Monastery. Six direct hits. You could see that. It just takes you a minute. Now, as to these structures here, I don't know what to say. Yes, of course, because the damage was the damage that was done, the hits were the hits; and as to the time, well, I think it's quite enough time to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you say that in one minute you can establish all the damage done by six hits, that one minute is enough for you to see how the impact took place, what the calibre of the weapon used, and can you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't speaking about calibres, that I could do that within a minute, but when you're passing by a balcony, a terrace, for example, and see four direct hits, in passing by, it's just six to eight metres, you can tell that, you can establish that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take a look at insula 11 now. So there were 11 different structures. Tell me, please, within those four hours, in addition to the 11 direct hits and five indirect hits with the 120-millimetre projectile, when you conducted your investigation you established two direct hits with incendiary bullets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you distinguish between an incendiary bullet and a non-incendiary bullet?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the point of impact, the incendiary bullet leaves a dark orange, reddish-orange colour trace. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a matter of translation. I just want to make sure there's consistency in the terminology that was used by the Translation Unit perhaps, and because I'm not sure that the term -- the term "incendiary" has been used previously, and "non-incendiary," but I'm not sure the word "bullet" has been used. Just so that we are certain that there is consistency with the terminology.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apologies: Projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now take a look, please, at number 7, insula 11. 69640 is the number, L006103 for the English version. And could you read the report to us, please. You can read it to yourself. You have it in front of you. Tell me, please, who provided you with the information for this particular structure? Who gave you the information about this?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone there to provide you with information?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember or do you not remember, or do you assume?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these forms, the number 9 structure was directly hit. So probably on structure 7, on the roof construction of number 7, there was some shrapnel from the projectile that fell there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me how you saw that if you didn't enter the structure. Is that your assumption?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have two neighbouring buildings, one hit by a 120-millimetre shell that fragmented and fell on the roof, then where would this other damage -- how would this other damage have been made but from that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you said it wasn't possible to investigate the structure. So you didn't actually enter the structure. And now I'm asking you how was it that you saw there was damage to the roof, or did you just assume that because the shell had fallen close by so most probably the roof of that particular house was damaged as well.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dubrovnik has higher house and lower houses, and if I went into the neighbouring structure, then I could look up and see, and there were buildings underneath the music school which stands at a higher altitude than all the other buildings. So that is something that I could have seen from the neighbouring building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about the details that I can't remember 12 and 13 years on. I can't remember specifically for this structure. I just recorded that there was nobody inside, in the building. So I don't write about the internal damages to the walls but the roof structure, which I was able to see, and you can be quite convinced that I haven't imagined or constructed or construed any data contained in my report. What I saw was enough for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're now making logical deductions and conclusions as to what could have happened but you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not making logical conclusions. Quite simply, my professional morals and ethics don't allow me to write down things that I didn't see. And we're dealing with damages. I'm not interested in the type and shape of the projectile at all, I'm interested in the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at 11/1, please, or -1. In the comment at the foot of the page, "Remarks," it says the building was repaired after the earthquake in 1979. Where do you get that piece of information, for example?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I worked in the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments, and I know that the building was included into the repair work that was done subsequent to the earthquake. And not only that, there was an additional part to the building that was built when the reconstruction was carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know about all the buildings that were repaired and reconstructed after the earthquake, the same thing that you said for the 11/1 building?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute has detailed information, but I do roughly know about the buildings that were repaired and reconstructed, especially the ones where I was the designer and architect working on the project. And in this particular case, it is reinforced concrete, and our constructions are generally -- the roof constructions are generally wooden constructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at the structure which has the number 10/10 now, please, which is 69643 page or, rather, for the English translation, L0061056.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the top, where it says "Type of projectile," you note that there were two pieces of 120-millimetre shells and two of 82 millimetres. In the comments or remarks at the bottom, it says: "The remains of one 120-millimetre shell were found." How were you then able to establish that there were four, that two were 120-millimetres and two were 82 millimetres, whereas at the bottom you just say you just found one fragment?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we looking at the same structure, 10/10?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did I say 10/10? I apologise. I meant 11/10. I apologise to the witness and to Their Honours. It is structure 11/10. And to my colleagues as well. It is 01069643 in the B/C/S, and the English version is L0061506. So we have two 120-millimetre projectiles, two 82-millimetre projectiles, whereas at the end, in the remarks, it says the fragments of one 120-millimetre shell were found. Now, my question to you is how were you able to establish that there were six hits of which two by 120 millimetre and two by 82 millimetres whereas you found just one 120-millimetre shell or, rather, the fragments of one such shell? If you don't know, then say you don't know and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, but I probably got the information from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't that seem to you to be rather strange?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't reconstruct the whole thing now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why in this case did you note down that fragments of a shell were found, of one shell were found?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why in the majority of other cases there are no remarks of that kind where you say the fragment of such-and-such shell found, just in this one case?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer that. I don't know. I can't go back 12 years to be able to explain that to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps because that was the only place you found any fragments, shell fragments.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no, no. You could come across them. People collected them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was this structure different from the others? Why did you write down that you found a shell fragment here whereas you didn't write that in any of the other cases? There must be some explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the explanation is that you didn't find anything like that in the other structures.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were shells all over the place. As many as you like. But as I have already told you, people would gather them up, collect them together, and keep them in one place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if the people stored them, why didn't you introduce that into your records, into your notes and minutes?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I told you that I was interested in the damage done and not in the shell that incurred the damage. And I don't like shells or anything like that. I don't even like picking them up, having them in my hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I trust you're keeping your eye on the time, are you, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. I do apologise, but I'm sure you'll understand this is extensive matter and that it is no easy task to find one's way in this bulk of material. I'm doing my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are no assessments of the damage in any of this material.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the object of the report. We were told that the damage would be evaluated in the final report and proposals for reconstruction and repair work to be done, that would be in the final report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume you don't know who established -- who evaluated and assessed the damage or how it was assessed. Do you have any personal experience of this? Any of your friends know about this that you can tell us, how the damage was assessed and evaluated?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I came across categories of damage. As to an evaluation of the damage, no, I didn't come across that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave elements for damage estimates? Have you heard about such things?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Well, maybe I did hear about it, but I don't remember at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When filling out these forms, did you fill them out in their entirety, every single entry? Was there perhaps something that you did not know or did you have to double-check something or did you always fill them out in their entirety?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would hand in the filled-out form. Possibly I did not even fill out some forms at all. For example, when a few of us were on this commission, only one of us would do the actual writing, not all three of us. We would establish what the damage was and then we would agree on what the text would be, and then one member of the commission would fill out the form. And it is certain that I let others write about types of projectiles, but at any rate, the form was always filled out. Sometimes I would put some comments in as well, like in the case of the school, that it had been reconstructed in 1979.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the reports that you compiled yourself, did you always fill out the entire form, every single question?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including those that had to do with the time when the building was hit, the type of projectile?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any dilemma as to what should be written down? Did you talk to someone? Did you seek advice?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always communicated amongst ourselves. We always talked. Before and after going on these tours, we talked about the buildings and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how data were included in every one of the maps that is attached to the report?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The data are based on the report that we provided, but in our form, there would be exact reference to the category involved, and then this would be depicted in the map. The locality of the damage was depicted by a symbol. I explained this to you at the very beginning, namely symbols showing the type of hit and the position of the building that was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you follow the drawing of these maps or did this happen after you submitted your report?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is only natural that the maps would be drawn after the report was submitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at binder number 1 now, the Franciscan Monastery. I have another question related to the city walls. There was a lot of damage there that was established; right? Is the answer yes?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how was information obtained there? Who provided the information? What was hit and when?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who dealt with this particular area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but if you don't know, let's just leave at it at that.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at 0106953. Please look at photograph number 11, if I'm not mistaken. That is a photograph 01069615. You looked at it awhile ago when my colleague showed it to you. My colleague showed you this photograph. Please take a look at the photograph.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, can you conclude on the basis of this photograph anything about the descent angle of the mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the exact route it took but perhaps the direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me on the basis of what you can establish the direction which it fell?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is the western wing of the cloister and behind it is the facade of the western wing of the monastery. The four shells were precisely in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this specific photograph and this that you can see here and now. Can you tell us the direction from which the shell fell? Yes or no. If you can't, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. And this photograph is so unclear anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please now take a look -- this is page 153. This is your report related to the Franciscan Monastery.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first sentence, you establish two direct hits on the facade of the western wing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- can you infer the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The eastern side, because, look, I can say this with certitude for one that hit the wall. The other one that hit the surrounding area I cannot say, but this one hit the corner between the southern and the western sides of the cloister. So it could have only come from the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, so you say that only on the basis of the fact that on the eastern side there were JNA units or why -- just let me finish my question, please. Do you infer that or conclude that on the basis of the fact that you believe the JNA units were there on the eastern side, or do you base your conclusion on your belief that you can tell the direction from which the shells were coming?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This has nothing to do with the side on which the JNA units were. It has to do with the position of the building and the place where the damage was sustained. If you have a wing which is on the west and if the south is there, then of course it -- the shell had to come from the east. There was no other way of having it happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you capable of ascertaining the direction from which the shell came on the basis of the actual damage?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, yes. It could have come from the north-east or east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in the next sentence you say the wall damaged where the southern and western wings come together.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where could it have come from?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I've been telling you all along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've read out your quote once again.

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, if this is the western wing and this is the southern wing, this western wing has its eastern facade and western facade, and the southern wing -- I mean, now we're talking about the building in general. This building has on the southern part a wall on the south and on the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did the shell come from, the one that hit the western facade of a particular building?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me look. The -- the two wings, the western and southern wing, and when we say "wing," we refer to a building, actually, so it was the eastern facade of the western wing. Look, can I draw this for you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please let me put the question and then you can answer it if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If I may just make an observation Your Honour. The witness was answering the question until my learned friend interrupted her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have understood the witness. I don't think that Mr. Petrovic has. Perhaps a drawing might help you, Mr. Petrovic, I leave it to you, but you are running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to put a question that is very simple and then a simple answer will do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If on a building, so we're not talking about the building right in front of us, if on a building the southern facade is damaged - not that building, I'm talking about a building - can you conclude from which direction the southern -- the shell came?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The southern facade? I can assume that it has to be 180 degrees in relation to the surface. Anywhere within that range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So anywhere -- any direction but the north; right?

utterances.speaker: LUCIJANA PEKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you please instruct me now? I have about half an hour of questioning left.
